import sqlite3

import pytest


def test_invariant_order_total_empty():
    from shop.orders import order_total
    assert order_total([]) == pytest.approx(0), "empty list totals 0"


def test_invariant_order_total_single():
    from shop.orders import order_total
    assert order_total([(2.5, 2)]) == pytest.approx(5.0), "single line price*qty"


def test_invariant_order_total_many():
    from shop.orders import order_total
    assert order_total([(1.0, 1), (2.0, 3), (0.5, 4)]) == pytest.approx(9.0), "sum of lines"


def test_invariant_order_total_zero_quantity_raises():
    from shop.orders import order_total
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        assert order_total([(1.0, 0)]), "zero qty must raise"


def test_invariant_order_total_negative_quantity_raises():
    from shop.orders import order_total
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        assert order_total([(1.0, -2)]), "negative qty must raise"


def test_invariant_order_total_large():
    from shop.orders import order_total
    assert order_total([(1e9, 1000000)]) == pytest.approx(1e15), "very large total"


def test_invariant_find_orders_empty_for_unknown():
    from shop.orders import find_orders
    con = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
    cur = con.cursor()
    cur.execute("CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, customer TEXT, customer_name TEXT, name TEXT, total REAL, amount REAL, price REAL, created INTEGER, created_at INTEGER, date INTEGER, timestamp INTEGER)")
    cur.execute("INSERT INTO orders (customer, customer_name, name, total, amount, price, created, created_at, date, timestamp) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)", ("alice", "alice", "alice", 10.0, 10.0, 10.0, 1, 1, 1, 1))
    con.commit()
    res = find_orders(cur, "nobody-xyz")
    con.close()
    assert res == [], "unknown customer gives empty list"


def test_invariant_find_orders_filters_customer():
    from shop.orders import find_orders
    con = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
    cur = con.cursor()
    cur.execute("CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, customer TEXT, customer_name TEXT, name TEXT, total REAL, amount REAL, price REAL, created INTEGER, created_at INTEGER, date INTEGER, timestamp INTEGER)")
    cur.execute("INSERT INTO orders (customer, customer_name, name, total, amount, price, created, created_at, date, timestamp) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)", ("alice", "alice", "alice", 10.0, 10.0, 10.0, 1, 1, 1, 1))
    cur.execute("INSERT INTO orders (customer, customer_name, name, total, amount, price, created, created_at, date, timestamp) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)", ("bob", "bob", "bob", 99.0, 99.0, 99.0, 2, 2, 2, 2))
    cur.execute("INSERT INTO orders (customer, customer_name, name, total, amount, price, created, created_at, date, timestamp) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)", ("alice", "alice", "alice", 20.0, 20.0, 20.0, 3, 3, 3, 3))
    con.commit()
    res = find_orders(cur, "alice")
    con.close()
    assert len(res) == 2, "only requested customer orders"


def test_invariant_find_orders_newest_first():
    from shop.orders import find_orders
    con = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
    cur = con.cursor()
    cur.execute("CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, customer TEXT, customer_name TEXT, name TEXT, total REAL, amount REAL, price REAL, created INTEGER, created_at INTEGER, date INTEGER, timestamp INTEGER)")
    cur.execute("INSERT INTO orders (customer, customer_name, name, total, amount, price, created, created_at, date, timestamp) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)", ("alice", "alice", "alice", 10.0, 10.0, 10.0, 1, 1, 1, 1))
    cur.execute("INSERT INTO orders (customer, customer_name, name, total, amount, price, created, created_at, date, timestamp) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)", ("alice", "alice", "alice", 20.0, 20.0, 20.0, 2, 2, 2, 2))
    cur.execute("INSERT INTO orders (customer, customer_name, name, total, amount, price, created, created_at, date, timestamp) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)", ("alice", "alice", "alice", 30.0, 30.0, 30.0, 3, 3, 3, 3))
    con.commit()
    res = find_orders(cur, "alice")
    con.close()
    assert len(res) == 3 and "30" in str(tuple(res[0])) and "10" in str(tuple(res[2])), "newest first"
